accounting: Two bases: reported (statutory) and proforma (Dealskart, GeoIQ, Meller consolidated in prior periods); the letters quote proforma growth, so Q1FY27 revenue growth is 33.6% proforma vs 43.3% reported.

EBITDA is after Ind AS 116 (rent excluded; right-of-use depreciation ₹704 cr and lease interest ₹163 cr in FY26). Lease principal paid ₹620 cr in FY26 sits in financing cash flow; we treat it as a cost of running stores.
FY25 profit includes a ₹167 cr non-cash gain on the Owndays deferred consideration (FY25 adjusted PAT ₹130 cr; the company's ₹2,140 Mn H1 and ₹5,300 Mn FY26 'adjusted PAT' are proforma).
Minority interests: ₹7.3 cr of FY26 profit (owners ₹493.6 cr of ₹501.0 cr); Screener's Net Profit is before minorities, so LENSKART.patch.js uses 'Profit for EPS'.
FY26 exceptional loss ₹15.7 cr (investment impairment ₹10.4 cr, IPO expenses ₹5.3 cr); FY26 other income includes ₹15.2 cr of liabilities written back and a ₹4.0 cr call-option fair-value gain.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Lenskart Solutions (consolidated, Rs crore). FY26 (Mar-2026) is the base year. Segment model: India and International revenue grow at the rates below; segment EBITDA (after Ind AS 116, before ESOP) is a margin on segment revenue; inter-segment sales are a negative segment with zero margin; consolidated EBITDA = segments less the inter-segment EBITDA elimination (unallocated) less ESOP. The India store build (net additions x revenue per store) is kept in storeBuild and checked against India revenue in LENSKART.ctx.js.

segments.name: India
segments._why: FY26 +29.5% (₹4,061 cr to ₹5,260 cr, AR FY26 note 41); Q1FY27 +30.7% (SSSG 18.3%, SPSG 24.3%, 116 net new stores). FY27E +29%: stores grow ~21% (store build) on top of SSSG in the mid-teens; Q1 SSSG was already 6 points below Q4FY26's 24.2%. FY28-29E +25% / +22%: management's ~25% volume yardstick, slower SSSG as the base matures and Tier 2+ stores (lower revenue per store) dominate openings.
segments._marginWhy: Segment EBITDA before ESOP was 12.3% of revenue in FY25 and 20.5% in FY26; Q1FY27 21.4% after ESOP (19.4% a year earlier). FY26 quarters rose from 19.4% (Q1) to 21.1% (Q4), so a full year runs ~1 point above Q1. We assume 22.3% / 23.3% / 24.2%: about 1 point a year from employee, marketing and rent leverage (Q4FY26 letter: 270 bp, 80 bp, 70 bp), partly reinvested in Tier 2+ staffing. Pre-IndAS this is ~16.5-18.5% against the ~25% long-term aim.

segments.name: International
segments._why: FY26 +36.7% (₹2,639 cr to ₹3,606 cr) with Meller added and rupee weakness; Q1FY27 +38.0% reported, ~29% in constant currency, with only 16 net new stores. FY27E +27%: constant-currency ~22-24% plus a fading currency gain; FY28-29E +20% / +18% (same-store led, Meller scaling towards ~US$70 mn, measured store additions).
segments._marginWhy: 19.3% before ESOP in FY26 (17.6% in FY25); Q1FY27 21.9% (16.9% a year earlier), helped by the sunglasses season; management asks investors to judge it on a trailing twelve-month basis. Pre-IndAS margin 3.6% (FY25), 7.0% (FY26), 10.6% (Q1FY27). We assume 21.0% / 21.8% / 22.5%: product-margin gains (77.1% in Q1FY27) and rent leverage, with marketing kept high.

segments.name: Inter-segment sales
segments._why: India sells frames and lenses to International: ₹46.7 cr in FY25, ₹52.1 cr in FY26 (~1% of India revenue), eliminated on consolidation. Grows with India.
segments._marginWhy: Zero: the margin effect is in the unallocated line.

assumptions._unallocWhy: Consolidated EBITDA less the two segments: +₹23 cr in FY25, −₹8 cr in FY26 (AR FY26 note 41: unrealised profit on inter-segment stock). We assume a ₹8 cr cost a year.
assumptions._esopWhy: Share-based payment ₹8.9 cr in FY25 and ₹12.8 cr in FY26 (AR FY26 note 27; standalone ₹9.0 cr). Small for a listed consumer-tech company. We assume ₹16 / 19 / 22 cr as grants under the 2021 plan continue (non-cash; added back to cash flow and equity).
assumptions._capexWhy: Cash capex plus the principal part of lease payments, because reported EBITDA excludes rent (ETERNAL/SWIGGY treatment). Cash capex: ₹416 cr in FY25, ₹828 cr in FY26 (stores, plant, Hyderabad land), ₹207 cr in Q1FY27 (stores ₹75 cr, plant ₹132 cr). Hyderabad (~₹1,500 cr estimated, foundation stone Mar-2025) is commissioning in ~18 months from May-2026 with a large part of the outlay in FY27. We assume cash capex ₹1,000 / 900 / 750 cr (plant ₹600 / 450 / 250 cr, stores and technology ₹400 / 450 / 500 cr for ~600 net new stores a year). Lease principal ₹469 cr (FY25), ₹620 cr (FY26); we assume ₹760 / 920 / 1,100 cr as the store base grows ~20% a year.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation ₹1,048 cr (right-of-use ₹704 cr, AR note 28) = 12.9% of average gross block (₹8,136 cr, Screener incl. right-of-use). Q1FY27 ₹305 cr (₹1,220 cr annualised, rising ~5% a quarter). 13.2% gives FY27E ~₹1,310 cr. The engine depreciates capex (including the lease-principal proxy for new right-of-use assets) at once; CWIP (₹112 cr) is held flat.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Applied to the model's opening net treasury: cash ₹1,544 cr + investments ₹571 cr + bank deposits in other financial assets ₹1,985 cr (otherTreasury) less borrowings including ₹2,877 cr of lease liabilities = ₹1,003 cr at Mar-2026. Bank deposits and debt funds earn ~6.5%.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Two parts, each sourced. (1) Income on the gross cash that the model nets against lease liabilities: the company's net cash was ₹3,881 cr at Mar-2026 (₹4,104 cr at Jun-2026) before leases, and 6.5% on the ₹2,877 cr lease offset = ₹187 cr. (2) Recurring non-treasury items, ₹24 cr in FY26 (AR note 25: security-deposit interest ₹7.4 cr, grants ₹6.1 cr, misc ₹7.0 cr, lease-termination gains ₹3.1 cr), ~₹25 cr. FY27E total ≈ ₹277 cr = Q1FY27's ₹69 cr annualised (₹276 cr). FY26's ₹174 cr is lower because the IPO cash arrived in Nov-2025 and includes ₹19 cr of one-offs (liabilities written back, call-option gain); the TTM to Jun-2026 is ₹186 cr.
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 ₹178 cr, of which lease interest ₹163 cr (AR note 29); Q1FY27 ₹53 cr (₹212 cr annualised). Lease interest grows with the store base (~20% a year); bank debt is small (₹220 cr).
assumptions._taxWhy: Q1FY27 24%, FY26 26.4% (incl. non-deductible IPO costs and impairment). India 25.17% regime plus higher-tax overseas units (Japan). The engine has no minority line, so we add ~1.5 points for minorities' share (2.1% of PAT in the year to Jun-2026, 1.5% in FY26): 26.5%.
assumptions._payoutWhy: No dividend since listing; cash goes to stores, Hyderabad and acquisitions (IPO objects include ₹683 cr for acquisitions and general purposes).

otherTreasury.label: Bank deposits held in other financial assets (treasury)
otherTreasury._why: Company-reported net cash ₹3,880.8 cr at Mar-2026 (Q4FY26 letter, excluding IPO-related payables) plus ₹219.6 cr of bank borrowings = ₹4,100 cr gross, less Screener's cash ₹1,544 cr and investments ₹571 cr. Matches AR note 7 (bank deposits due within 12 months ₹1,976 cr, NBFC deposits ₹10.6 cr) and note 6 (long deposits ₹26.9 cr).

storeBuild._why: India stores: 2,067 (Mar-25), 2,609 (Mar-26), 2,725 (Jun-26). Net additions FY27 'at or around FY26 levels' (company); we assume 540 / 560 / 580 in India. India revenue per average store rose 6.7% in FY26 (₹2.25 cr on 2,338 average stores vs ₹2.11 cr; India revenue includes online, ~50% digitally influenced). We assume +4.8% / +5.0% / +4.6% (SSSG in the mid-teens diluted by young Tier 2+ stores, which start at ~₹16-18 lakh a month, i.e. ~₹2 cr a year), which must reproduce the India growth above within 1.5 points (checked in LENSKART.ctx.js).

dcf._betaWhy: Discretionary-medical retail with high growth and a short listed history: beta 1.0, cost of equity 12.5%. Bank debt is negligible; lease liabilities are deducted as debt, so the cost of equity is the discount rate.
dcf._tgWhy: Eyewear is under-penetrated (78 cr Indians need correction, ~35% use glasses, company) and premiumising: 6%, the top of the house range.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~20% in FY29E to 9% by FY42E.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA (post-IndAS) fades up to 27% of revenue: consistent with the ~25% pre-IndAS long-term aim less ~6-8 points of rent that sits in depreciation and interest, but below a full delivery of it.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex including lease principal fades from ~11% of revenue (FY29E) to 8% (cash capex ~3%, leases ~5%); depreciation incl. right-of-use 7.5% of revenue long run (11.9% in FY26).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: India SSSG stays near 20% and Tier 2+ stores ramp like the older ones; International keeps compounding at 25% with Meller and the Middle East; operating leverage takes segment EBITDA ~1.5 points above our base by FY29E; Hyderabad brings frames and lenses in-house on time.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Store additions outrun demand: SSSG drops to high single digits, Tier 2+ stores mature at lower revenue; the rupee keeps weakening against the RMB/yen (imported frames), squeezing product margin; International margins slip back towards FY26 levels as marketing stays high.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: How the street values Lenskart: EV/EBITDA, 1.5-2 years forward (MOFSL 49x Sep-28E, Emkay 56x Jun-28E, Equirus 58x, Jefferies/Elara 50x FY28E, all on pre-IndAS EBITDA; JM and ICICI Securities DCF-implied 48-53x). We apply the multiple to reported (post-IndAS) EBITDA with lease liabilities in net debt, the basis on which the stock's own history can be measured. Derived in LENSKART.ctx.js (own forward EV/EBITDA median since listing x the retail peers' EV/EBITDA move over the same window) and written by LENSKART.val.js.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: Own forward P/E median since listing x the retail peers' P/E move over the same window (LENSKART.ctx.js).

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF (lease principal treated as capex), cost of equity 12.5%, terminal growth 6%.

rentBuild._why: Rent under Ind AS 116 = lease principal + lease interest (cash), used only to translate our post-IndAS EBITDA into the pre-IndAS (after-rent) EBITDA the street values. FY25 ₹469 + ₹125 cr, FY26 ₹620 + ₹163 cr (AR FY26 cash flow); Q1FY27 rent implied by the company's two EBITDA figures ₹227 cr (₹588 cr less ₹361 cr). Lease principal as in capex; lease interest = finance cost less ~₹15 cr of other interest.

cover.headline: India's eyewear category-builder: a better business every quarter, but the price already runs ahead of it
cover.lead: Lenskart designs, makes and sells glasses through 3,459 stores (2,725 in India) and an app, and owns Owndays (Japan) and Meller (Spain). It listed on 10-Nov-2025 at ₹402; the stock has risen 70% since. FY26 revenue grew 32.5% to ₹8,814 cr and EBITDA margin reached 19.9% (13.3% after rent in Q1FY27, against a ~25% long-term aim). We forecast EPS of ₹5.05 / ₹6.94 / ₹9.29 for FY27-29E, in the middle of the street. The street values Lenskart on **EV/EBITDA 1.5-2 years forward** (48-58x EBITDA after rent). The house rule (its own forward EV/EBITDA median since listing, 30.6x, adjusted by the retail peers' −11.6% move over the same ten months) gives **27x Sep-28E EBITDA of ₹3,540 cr = {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with SELL.** That is ≈41.2x after-rent EBITDA on the street's basis. Cross-checks: P/E ₹592, DCF ₹402. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: The business is creating its own market, and it shows in the numbers
arguments.p: India revenue +30.7% in Q1FY27 with SSSG 18.3%, 63 lakh eye tests (+43%, half first-ever) and 116 net new stores; ~6,100 Indian pin codes still have no Lenskart store. Product margin crossed 70% as frames and lenses moved in-house. We model India +{{as.segments.0.growth.0|pct0}} / +{{as.segments.0.growth.1|pct0}} / +{{as.segments.0.growth.2|pct0}} on ~560 openings a year.

International (41% of revenue) went from a 3.6% margin after rent in FY25 to 7.0% in FY26 and 10.6% in Q1FY27, on same-store growth (+38%, ~29% in constant currency) with only 16 new stores. Meller is tracking towards ~US$70 mn. We take 21.0% before rent and ESOP in FY27E (Q1 is the sunglasses season).

Reported EBITDA (21.7% in Q1FY27) excludes rent under Ind AS 116; after rent the margin is 13.3%. On our numbers after-rent EBITDA rises from ~₹971 cr in FY26 to ₹2,533 cr in FY29E (~15.1% of revenue). Operating leverage is real, but SSSG is cooling (24% to 18% in two quarters) and openings move to smaller towns.

arguments.h: Valuation: the street pays for the next decade today
arguments.p: At ₹685.05 the stock trades at 33.4x Sep-28E EBITDA before rent and 98.7x FY28E EPS, above its 30.6x forward median since listing, while retail peers trade ~12% below their own medians over the same months. The street's median target (₹707, 12 post-results notes) needs 48-58x after-rent EBITDA. Pre-IPO funds (SoftBank, ADIA, Alpha Wave) have been selling into strength since May.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): India SSSG after 18.3% in Q1, International margin after the sunglasses season, store additions against the ~600 plan.
Further block sales by pre-IPO holders (SoftBank 7.3%, ADIA, PI Opportunities Fund, Macritchie, Steadview): supply on rallies.
Hyderabad plant (~18 months from May-2026): capex peak in FY27, then product-margin gains.
Acquisitions funded from the ₹683 cr IPO allocation and the ₹4,104 cr net cash.
Smart glasses (B by Lenskart): 80,000+ sign-ups by Aug-2026; no revenue in our model.

blocks.callout: **How it makes money:** Lenskart earns a ~70% product margin (revenue less the cost of frames and lenses) because it designs, makes and sells its own glasses: the Bhiwadi plant makes frames and lenses for India and much of International, and a central lab ships made-to-order glasses next day in 78 cities. From that margin it pays staff (optometrists in every store), rent and marketing. Every eye test is the top of the funnel: 23.8 mn in FY26, about half of them first-ever tests in India. Gold, a paid membership (8.8 mn members, ₹200 cr of fees in FY26), keeps customers coming back.

blocks.callout: **Why it matters:** about 40% of revenue and most of the goodwill came through acquisitions, and the FY25-26 franchise buy-back changed the cost structure (commissions down, staff and rent up). The clean, like-for-like history is short: the company itself presents "proforma" numbers to bridge it. Lenskart has shown it can integrate (Owndays' margin is up, Meller has doubled), but acquisitions remain part of the plan.

sections.title: India needs 78 cr pairs of eyes corrected and only 35% of them wear glasses: a market that grows by being created

blocks.p: The company's own build of the Indian market (AR FY26, using Redseer and government data): 145 cr people, 53% needing vision correction (77.7 cr), only 35% of them actually using correction (27.4 cr), 0.88 pairs a year each: 24.2 cr pairs at ~₹2,370 = ₹573 bn of prescription eyewear in FY25, ₹788 bn including contact lenses and sunglasses (₹894 bn estimated for FY26). By FY30 it projects 62% needing correction, 41% penetration, ₹1,478 bn. India imported 44 cr ophthalmic lenses in FY25 (~22 cr pairs), up 11% a year in volume since FY19 (DGCIS).

Most of the market is still unorganised: neighbourhood opticians who buy frames and lenses from wholesalers and test eyes by hand. Lenskart had a 4-6% share of Indian prescription eyewear in FY25 (RHP via ICICI Direct, 30-Oct-2025). Abroad, its markets (South-East Asia, Japan, Middle East) were a ₹1,716 bn eyewear market in FY26, growing 7-10% a year in Japan, 10-14% in South-East Asia and 15-20% in the Middle East for organised and direct-to-consumer players; in Japan the direct-to-consumer share rose from 25% to 31% in five years and Owndays is the third-largest such chain with 287 stores against 500+ each for the top two (AR FY26).

blocks.p: Under Ind AS 116, store rent is not an operating expense: it becomes depreciation of a "right-of-use" asset plus interest on a lease liability. Lenskart's reported EBITDA (21.7% in Q1FY27) therefore excludes rent; its "EBITDA pre-IndAS 116" (13.3%) deducts it. The gap (~8 points) is the rent bill. blocks.callout: **Verdict:** Lenskart has a genuine cost and reach advantage over unorganised opticians, which is where its share gains come from. It is a narrow moat in a fragmented market: it does not give pricing power, and returns depend on executing ~600 openings a year without hurting service. That is enough to justify a premium retail multiple; it is not a platform-style moat.

sections.title: Revenue up 2.3x in three years and EBITDA margin from 7% to 20%: Lenskart has crossed from losses to scale profits

blocks.p: Revenue went from ₹3,788 cr in FY23 (the first year with Owndays, which lifted revenue 152%) to ₹8,814 cr in FY26, 32.5% a year. EBITDA rose from ₹264 cr to ₹1,754 cr and the margin from 7.0% to 19.9% (after Ind AS 116, i.e. before rent; the company's own pre-IndAS 116 EBITDA, after rent, passed ₹1,000 cr in FY26, ~11% of revenue). Net profit after minorities went from a ₹64 cr loss in FY23 to ₹494 cr in FY26; FY25's ₹296 cr includes a ₹167 cr non-cash gain on the Owndays deferred consideration, so the underlying FY25 profit was ~₹130 cr. Three things drove the margin: product margin (revenue less materials) up from 64% to 71% as frames and lenses moved in-house; the switch from franchise (FoFo) to company stores (CoCo), which cut commissions from ₹733 cr to ₹181 cr while staff costs rose; and operating leverage on stores, marketing and head office.

sections.title: Clean audit; three adjustments: proforma vs reported, rent outside EBITDA, and a one-off in FY25

bullets: **Two sets of numbers.** The letters quote "proforma" growth (Dealskart, GeoIQ and Meller consolidated in the base year); the audited accounts are "reported". From Q3FY26 the two are identical, but FY26 growth rates differ (Q1FY27 revenue +33.6% proforma, +43.3% reported). We use reported figures in the model and say when we quote proforma.

**EBITDA excludes rent.** Ind AS 116 moves rent into depreciation (right-of-use ₹704 cr) and interest (₹163 cr) and the cash into financing (lease principal ₹620 cr). Operating cash flow (₹1,670 cr) therefore overstates cash earnings; we treat lease principal as capex in the forecasts.

**FY25 one-off.** FY25 other income includes a ₹167 cr non-cash gain on the Owndays deferred consideration; FY26 includes ₹19 cr of liabilities written back and a call-option gain, and a ₹16 cr exceptional loss (investment impairment, IPO costs). Our forecasts carry none of these.
**Minorities.** ₹7.3 cr of FY26 profit and ~₹6-7 cr in Q1FY27 belong to minority partners; we use profit after minorities (LENSKART.patch.js) and load ~1.5 points onto the tax rate in forecasts.
**ESOP cost is small** (₹12.8 cr in FY26) because most options were granted before the IPO; grants at listed-market prices would raise it. We deduct ₹{{as.esop.0|num}}-{{as.esop.2|num}} cr a year.
**Goodwill** (₹2,198 cr) and brands (₹980 cr) from Owndays and Meller are tested for impairment yearly; no impairment of goodwill in FY26.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: GREEN-AMBER (we show AMBER).** S.R. Batliboi (EY) audits the accounts and we found nothing improper. The amber reflects the short like-for-like history, the proforma presentation in the letters and a headline EBITDA that excludes the largest store cost.

blocks.p: Coverage began after the IPO quiet period (Jefferies, Macquarie, Emkay and Avendus in Nov-Dec 2025; Ambit published a Sell before listing) and widened in 2026 (Antique, Motilal Oswal, Elara, CLSA, BofA, J.P. Morgan, Nomura, ICICI Securities). After the Q1FY27 results (12-Aug-2026) 12 houses published dated targets: median ₹707 (+3% vs the 30-Sep-2026 close of ₹685.05); including the older notes still standing, the median is ₹663. 9 are Buy or equivalent, Citi and HSBC are neutral and Ambit is the lone Sell (₹496). Every multiple we could confirm is EV/EBITDA on pre-IndAS (after-rent) EBITDA 1.5-2 years forward: Motilal Oswal 49x Sep-28E, Emkay 56x Jun-28E, Equirus 58x, Jefferies and Elara 50x FY28E; JM Financial (DCF, 53x implied) and ICICI Securities (DCF, ~48x India implied). Nobody uses P/E or EV/Sales as the main method; Bloomberg consensus P/E was 119x / 87x one/two-year forward (Motilal Oswal, 9-Sep-2026).

Bloomberg consensus (Motilal Oswal, 9-Sep-2026): post-IndAS EBITDA ₹2,726 cr / ₹3,460 cr and PAT ₹1,011 cr / ₹1,391 cr one/two years forward; EV/EBITDA 44.4x / 35.0x, P/E 119x / 87x at ₹692. 20 analysts on Bloomberg, 10 Buy (Business Today, 13-Aug-2026).

blocks.p: The street uses EV/EBITDA on EBITDA after rent ("pre-IndAS 116"), 1.5-2 years forward, at 48-58x. We use the same method on the same date (Sep-28E: half FY28E, half FY29E) but on reported EBITDA before rent, with lease liabilities (₹2,877 cr at Mar-2026) counted as debt. The two are equivalent ways of treating rent; ours is the one on which the stock's own history and our model can be measured consistently. To compare, our target equals **41.2x** Sep-28E EBITDA after rent (₹2,255 cr, our estimate) on the street's basis. The "At our EBITDA" column applies each broker's multiple to our after-rent EBITDA.

sections.title: Our honest summary: a strong business at 33.4x Sep-28E EBITDA; SELL on valuation, not on quality

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's largest organised eyewear company, growing ~30% with ~600 new stores a year, a ~70% product margin from its own factories, an International business that has just become properly profitable (10.6% margin after rent in Q1FY27), ₹4,104 cr of net cash and a long runway (4-6% share of a market that is itself being created). The quality is not in question.

**What you are paying:** ₹685.05 is 135.7x our FY27E and 98.7x FY28E EPS, and 33.4x Sep-28E EBITDA before rent (≈50.1x after rent on the street's basis). Since listing the stock has traded at a median 30.6x forward EBITDA; retail multiples have fallen ~12% over the same months. The street (median ₹707) pays 48-58x after-rent EBITDA, a premium the stock's own short history and the sector's de-rating do not support under our rule.

We assume cash capex ₹1,000 / 900 / 750 cr (plant ₹600 / 450 / 250 cr, stores and technology ₹400 / 450 / 500 cr for ~600 net new stores a year). Lease principal ₹469 cr (FY25), ₹620 cr (FY26); we assume ₹760 / 920 / 1,100 cr as the store base grows ~20% a year.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation ₹1,048 cr (right-of-use ₹704 cr, AR note 28) = 12.9% of average gross block (₹8,136 cr, Screener incl. right-of-use). Q1FY27 ₹305 cr (₹1,220 cr annualised, rising ~5% a quarter). 13.2% gives FY27E ~₹1,310 cr. The engine depreciates capex (including the lease-principal proxy for new right-of-use assets) at once; CWIP (₹112 cr) is held flat.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Applied to the model's opening net treasury: cash ₹1,544 cr + investments ₹571 cr + bank deposits in other financial assets ₹1,985 cr (otherTreasury) less borrowings including ₹2,877 cr of lease liabilities = ₹1,003 cr at Mar-2026. Bank deposits and debt funds earn ~6.5%.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Two parts, each sourced. (1) Income on the gross cash that the model nets against lease liabilities: the company's net cash was ₹3,881 cr at Mar-2026 (₹4,104 cr at Jun-2026) before leases, and 6.5% on the ₹2,877 cr lease offset = ₹187 cr. (2) Recurring non-treasury items, ₹24 cr in FY26 (AR note 25: security-deposit interest ₹7.4 cr, grants ₹6.1 cr, misc ₹7.0 cr, lease-termination gains ₹3.1 cr), ~₹25 cr. FY27E total ≈ ₹277 cr = Q1FY27's ₹69 cr annualised (₹276 cr). FY26's ₹174 cr is lower because the IPO cash arrived in Nov-2025 and includes ₹19 cr of one-offs (liabilities written back, call-option gain); the TTM to Jun-2026 is ₹186 cr.
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 ₹178 cr, of which lease interest ₹163 cr (AR note 29); Q1FY27 ₹53 cr (₹212 cr annualised). Lease interest grows with the store base (~20% a year); bank debt is small (₹220 cr).
assumptions._taxWhy: Q1FY27 24%, FY26 26.4% (incl. non-deductible IPO costs and impairment). India 25.17% regime plus higher-tax overseas units (Japan). The engine has no minority line, so we add ~1.5 points for minorities' share (2.1% of PAT in the year to Jun-2026, 1.5% in FY26): 26.5%.
assumptions._payoutWhy: No dividend since listing; cash goes to stores, Hyderabad and acquisitions (IPO objects include ₹683 cr for acquisitions and general purposes).

otherTreasury.label: Bank deposits held in other financial assets (treasury)
otherTreasury._why: Company-reported net cash ₹3,880.8 cr at Mar-2026 (Q4FY26 letter, excluding IPO-related payables) plus ₹219.6 cr of bank borrowings = ₹4,100 cr gross, less Screener's cash ₹1,544 cr and investments ₹571 cr. Matches AR note 7 (bank deposits due within 12 months ₹1,976 cr, NBFC deposits ₹10.6 cr) and note 6 (long deposits ₹26.9 cr).

storeBuild._why: India stores: 2,067 (Mar-25), 2,609 (Mar-26), 2,725 (Jun-26). Net additions FY27 'at or around FY26 levels' (company); we assume 540 / 560 / 580 in India. India revenue per average store rose 6.7% in FY26 (₹2.25 cr on 2,338 average stores vs ₹2.11 cr; India revenue includes online, ~50% digitally influenced). We assume +4.8% / +5.0% / +4.6% (SSSG in the mid-teens diluted by young Tier 2+ stores, which start at ~₹16-18 lakh a month, i.e. ~₹2 cr a year), which must reproduce the India growth above within 1.5 points (checked in LENSKART.ctx.js).

dcf._betaWhy: Discretionary-medical retail with high growth and a short listed history: beta 1.0, cost of equity 12.5%. Bank debt is negligible; lease liabilities are deducted as debt, so the cost of equity is the discount rate.
dcf._tgWhy: Eyewear is under-penetrated (78 cr Indians need correction, ~35% use glasses, company) and premiumising: 6%, the top of the house range.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~20% in FY29E to 9% by FY42E.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA (post-IndAS) fades up to 27% of revenue: consistent with the ~25% pre-IndAS long-term aim less ~6-8 points of rent that sits in depreciation and interest, but below a full delivery of it.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex including lease principal fades from ~11% of revenue (FY29E) to 8% (cash capex ~3%, leases ~5%); depreciation incl. right-of-use 7.5% of revenue long run (11.9% in FY26).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: India SSSG stays near 20% and Tier 2+ stores ramp like the older ones; International keeps compounding at 25% with Meller and the Middle East; operating leverage takes segment EBITDA ~1.5 points above our base by FY29E; Hyderabad brings frames and lenses in-house on time.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Store additions outrun demand: SSSG drops to high single digits, Tier 2+ stores mature at lower revenue; the rupee keeps weakening against the RMB/yen (imported frames), squeezing product margin; International margins slip back towards FY26 levels as marketing stays high.
